$comment: OUT-001 (D-72): the single source of ISEDRAF exit codes. OWNER-CONTROLLED (CLAUDE.md section 1). Code, documentation and tests are validated against it by scripts/ci/check_exitcodes.py in make check. It consolidates the codes already admitted by OUT-001, SCOPE-077, AUTH-023 and AUTH-020; it defines no new code. `reachable` says whether this version can return the code; the comparison and baseline codes are frozen and not reachable before v0.4.

codes.name: OK
codes.meaning: the run or report completed and every area was COLLECTED; nothing unaccepted

codes.name: INCOMPLETE
codes.meaning: the run or report completed, but some area is PARTIAL, NOT_TESTED or ERROR (or NOT_COMPARABLE in tracked sections)

codes.name: USAGE_OR_ENGINE
codes.meaning: usage error or engine error; nothing was committed

codes.name: RUN_IN_PROGRESS
codes.meaning: the whole-run lock was not acquired; nothing was collected or written

codes.name: STATE_ROOT_UNUSABLE
codes.meaning: the state root cannot be used (missing, not a conforming directory, a link, wrong owner or mode, not writable, unsuitable storage); detected before any collection

codes.name: PRIVILEGE_REFUSED
codes.meaning: root or sudo invocation refused; nothing was collected

signal_statuses.$comment: Not ISEDRAF codes: the shell convention 128 + N that the Full Audit outer entry returns after an interruption, and the status a unit stopped before it could handle the stop ends with (AUTH-020, IQ-063). Numerically above 64; they never mean a usage or engine error.

statuses.meaning: interrupted before the commit; nothing was committed (or no claim, with a notice saying so)
interrupted before the commit; nothing was committed (or no claim, with a notice saying so)
interrupted before the commit; nothing was committed (also the unit's own status when it is stopped before its commit)
the Full Audit unit ended abnormally (stopped before it could handle the stop); no claim about what was committed
